evidence.claim: TAL-24 cached computed invoice totals to speed up the list page, shipped, then was reverted after totals went stale when line items changed.
TAL-68 has acceptance criteria (totals served from cache, list under one second) but none cover invalidation when line items change.
TAL-64 covers the same slow invoice list problem (6 seconds for over 10,000 invoices) and is still open, so it overlaps only in goal.

body.why: Risky: TAL-24 cached the same invoice totals in memcached and was reverted because totals went stale when line items changed. TAL-68 swaps in Redis and doesn't say how it avoids the same staleness.
wouldChange: Add an acceptance criterion and a plan for invalidating cached totals when line items change, which addresses the reason TAL-24 was reverted.
Confirm the Redis approach differs from TAL-24 in a way that prevents stale totals, then it can move to Ready to Build.

check.reason: Verdict and rejected outcome both verify.
